name: Mont-Saint-Michel Abbey
note: The item is the abbey on the island, which a Benedictine community still keeps; the sources name the island as a whole, and the abbey is what the pilgrimage there goes to.

name: Sainte-Chapelle
note: A palace chapel visited mainly for its glass and run as a monument; kept because it is a consecrated chapel and both sources name it as a place of worship.

name: Basilica of St. Francis of Assisi
Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba
note: A cathedral since 1236 in the former great mosque; the mosque lists name it as a mosque and the church lists as a church, and it is one place either way.

name: Montserrat Abbey
note: The Benedictine abbey on the mountain, which keeps the Black Madonna that pilgrims come for.

name: Hagia Sophia
note: A working mosque again since 2020, after centuries as a cathedral and decades as a museum; a traveller visits it outside prayer times.

name: Meteora
note: The item is the rock formation with its cluster of monasteries, which is how every source names the place; six of the monasteries are inhabited and open to visitors.

name: Mount Athos
note: The item is the monastic community of the Holy Mountain, not the summit alone. Entry is by a pilgrim's permit, for men only, and a limited number a day; the canon keeps it because pilgrimage is exactly how it is visited.

name: Spanish Synagogue, Prague
note: Run by the Jewish Museum in Prague as an exhibition hall and concert venue. Kept because both sources name it as a place of worship.

name: Dome of the Rock
note: A shrine, not a mosque, on the Haram al-Sharif (Temple Mount); non-Muslims may enter the esplanade at set hours but not the building.

name: Al-Aqsa Mosque
note: The item is the congregational mosque (the prayer hall) on the Haram al-Sharif, not the whole compound; non-Muslims see it from the esplanade.

name: Saint Catherine's Monastery
note: At the foot of Mount Sinai, in the Asian part of Egypt.

name: Church of Saint George, Lalibela
note: The own list named the eleven rock-hewn churches of Lalibela as a group; Touropia names this one, Bete Giyorgis, the cross-shaped church that stands for the group. The item is the church itself, so visiting another of the eleven is not a visit to it.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá
note: An underground church in a salt mine; it is consecrated and Mass is still said there.

name: Masjid al-Haram
note: Open to Muslims only, as is all of Mecca; it is the destination of the Hajj and the Umrah, which is the visit the canon means. Explore.com names the Kaaba inside it, which is not counted for the mosque.

name: Prophet's Mosque
note: In Medina; a pilgrimage destination for Muslims, most of whom join it to the Hajj or the Umrah.

name: Great Mosque of Djenné
note: Non-Muslims are not admitted inside; the visit is its outside and the market square in front of it.

name: Shah Mosque, Isfahan
note: Also called the Imam Mosque, on Naqsh-e Jahan Square.

name: Imam Reza Shrine
note: A Shia shrine and the largest pilgrimage site in Iran; non-Muslims may enter the courtyards with a guide but not the inner sanctuary.

name: Jameh Mosque of Isfahan
note: Not on the own list; Rough Guides, SURFIRAN and Le Routard name it.

name: Muhammad Ali Mosque
note: The mosque on the Cairo Citadel.

name: Shah-i-Zinda
note: A necropolis of mausoleums around the shrine of Qusam ibn Abbas, still a place of pilgrimage and prayer; it is of this kind as a saint's shrine people pray at.

name: Jagannath Temple, Puri
note: Only Hindus may enter; the visit for others is the outside, the temple kitchen's surroundings and the Rath Yatra.

name: Swaminarayan Akshardham, Delhi
note: The own list named it twice (as Akshardham and as Swaminarayan Akshardham); counted once.

name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
note: A group of temples visited mostly for their sculpture; kept because worship continues at the Matangeshvara temple and in the Jain group, and the sources name it as temples. In doubt, kept.

name: Prambanan Temple
note: A 9th-century complex restored from ruin; kept, as the kind's definition keeps it, because Hindu ceremonies are held there again, notably before Nyepi.

name: Tanah Lot
note: The Wikidata item is the rock with its sea temple, typed as a Balinese Hindu temple; there is no separate item for the temple.

name: Pashupatinath Temple
note: Only Hindus may enter the main temple; the visit for others is the riverbank complex and the cremation ghats.

name: Batu Caves
note: The item is the limestone hill whose caves hold the temples, which is how both sources name it.

name: Borobudur
note: The item is the temple itself, not the World Heritage compound with Mendut and Pawon. Restored from ruin and visited mostly as a monument, but Vesak is celebrated there each year; kept, as the kind's definition keeps it.

name: Angkor Wat
note: The temple, not the Angkor park; Buddhist monks still worship there. Insight Guides names "Angkor", counted here because its text is the temple's.

name: Potala Palace
note: A palace and monastery, the Dalai Lamas' former seat, now a museum the state runs; kept because Tibetan pilgrims still walk its circuit and pray in its chapels.

name: Temple of Heaven
note: A state altar where emperors prayed for harvests; no rites are held now, and it is a park. Kept because the kind names a state altar.

name: Wat Phra Kaew
note: The temple of the Emerald Buddha inside the Grand Palace; Explore.com and Touropia name the Grand Palace, which is not counted for it.

name: Wat Rong Khun
note: A modern temple an artist has been building since 1997; it is a consecrated Buddhist temple, not an art installation.

name: Paro Taktsang (Tiger's Nest)
note: Not on the own list; three publishers name it.

name: Ise Grand Shrine
note: The item is Ise Jingū as a whole; japan-guide names its Inner Shrine (and, separately, the Outer Shrine), both of which the item contains.

name: Dohány Street Synagogue
note: Touropia names it the Great Synagogue.

name: São Francisco Church and Convent, Salvador
note: The church of the Franciscan convent, not the Third Order church beside it, which has its own item.

name: Pantheon, Rome
note: An ancient Roman temple that has been a church (Santa Maria ad Martyres) since 609 and still holds Mass; most visitors come for the building, but it is a consecrated basilica.

name: Chora Church
note: A Byzantine church, then a mosque, then a museum, and a mosque again since 2024; visited for its mosaics and frescoes.

name: Saint Isaac's Cathedral
note: Run as a state museum, with services held in it.

name: Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood
note: Run as a state museum, with services held in it.

name: Wieskirche
note: The pilgrimage church at Steingaden, Bavaria.

name: Rila Monastery
note: The item is the monastery itself, not the World Heritage ensemble item.

name: Speyer Cathedral
note: Not on the own list; Rough Guides and MERIAN both name it.

name: Hallgrímskirkja
note: Not on the own list; Touropia and Travel365 both name it.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of the Pillar
note: Not on the own list; the great Marian pilgrimage church of Zaragoza.

name: Alcobaça Monastery
note: Not on the own list. A Cistercian abbey visited mostly as a monument; its church is still used for worship, and both sources name it as a monastery.

name: Basilica of San Vitale
note: Not on the own list. Visited for its mosaics on a museum ticket, but a consecrated basilica, and both sources name it as a place of worship.

name: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes
note: The item is the whole sanctuary. Le Routard's Lourdes page names its parts: the grotto of Massabielle and the basilicas of the Immaculate Conception and of the Rosary, all within it.

name: Old New Synagogue
note: Still a working synagogue, the oldest in Europe in use.

name: Geghard
note: The monastery, partly carved into the rock; the village of the same name has its own item.

name: Etchmiadzin Cathedral
note: Le Routard names the town, Etchmiadzin, as the seat of the Armenian Apostolic Church; the item is its mother cathedral, which is what that visit is to.

name: Khor Virap
note: Not on the own list; Touropia and Le Routard both name it. A monastery and pilgrimage site under Mount Ararat.

name: Shrine of the Báb
note: Le Routard names it with its terraced gardens. The item is the shrine itself; the gardens are the setting of the visit.

name: Church of Nosso Senhor do Bonfim
note: Not on the own list; Melhores Destinos and Le Routard both name it. The pilgrimage church of Salvador, Bahia, known for its ribbons and the washing of its steps.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace, Yamoussoukro
Kul Sharif Mosque
note: In the Kazan Kremlin; rebuilt and opened in 2005.

name: Selimiye Mosque
note: In Edirne.

name: Vank Cathedral
note: Not on the own list; the Armenian cathedral of Isfahan, still in use, which both Iranian sources name.

name: Virupaksha Temple, Hampi
note: Not on the own list. The one temple of Hampi still in worship, unlike the ruined city around it.

name: Shwezigon Pagoda
note: A working pagoda in Bagan; the canon keeps it on its own, not the Bagan zone.

name: Byōdō-in
note: The temple at Uji, not the replica in Hawaii that Explore.com names.

name: Kōtoku-in (Great Buddha of Kamakura)
note: Not on the own list; Explore.com and japan-guide.com both name it, the latter as the Great Buddha.

name: Uluru
note: Not on the own list; Touring Club Italiano and Le Routard both name it among sacred places. A rock sacred to the Anangu, venerated as a place, the kind's holy-mountain case; climbing it has been closed since 2019 and the visit is the base walk and the view.
